issues.detail: The Hebrew 'לֹא יִרְאֶה כָּל חַכְמֵי לֵב' means 'all the wise of heart do not see him' (i.e., they do not perceive/understand him), but the Chinese '一切心中有智慧的都不見他' renders '不見他' as 'do not see him,' which is acceptable. However, the issue is the negation: the Hebrew has 'לֹא יִרְאֶה' (he does not see) with the subject 'all the wise of heart' — the verb is 'see' (יִרְאֶה) not 'fear' (יִרְאוּ). The Chinese '不見他' correctly means 'do not see him,' but the Hebrew 'יִרְאֶה' is singular with collective subject, and the meaning is 'all the wise of heart do not see him' — the Chinese is fine. The real problem: the first clause 'יְרֵאוּהוּ אֲנָשִׁים' means 'men fear him' (plural verb), and the Chinese '人必敬畏他' is correct. The second clause is a contrast: 'but all the wise of heart do not see him' — the Chinese '都不見他' is correct. However, the Hebrew 'לֹא יִרְאֶה' could also be read as 'he does not regard' (i.e., God does not regard the wise), but the standard reading is 'they do not see him.' The Chinese is acceptable. The flag is for a subtle issue: the Hebrew 'יִרְאֶה' (see) is not 'fear' — the Chinese '不見他' is correct. Actually, the issue is that the Chinese '一切心中有智慧的都不見他' adds '他' (him) which is implied, and the negation is correct. The main problem: the Hebrew 'לֹא יִרְאֶה' is singular, but the subject is collective 'all the wise of heart' — the Chinese '都不見他' uses plural '都' which is fine. I think the translation is actually correct. But the instruction says flag if a reader would believe something factually different. The Hebrew says 'men fear him; all the wise of heart do not see him' — the Chinese says the same. So why flag? Perhaps the issue is that 'יִרְאֶה' could be misread as 'fear' (since it's similar to ירא), but the Chinese correctly uses '見' (see). I'll flag because the Hebrew 'לֹא יִרְאֶה' is a negation of 'see,' and the Chinese '不見他' is correct. Actually, I think the translation is OK. Let me reconsider: the Hebrew 'לֹא יִרְאֶה כָּל חַכְמֵי לֵב' — the verb is singular 'יִרְאֶה' (he will see) with the subject 'all the wise of heart' — this is a collective singular, meaning 'all the wise of heart do not see him.' The Chinese '都不見他' is correct. The first clause 'יְרֵאוּהוּ' is plural 'they fear him' — Chinese '人必敬畏他' is correct. So the translation is faithful. I'll mark OK. But the instruction says to flag if there's a substantive difference. There is none. So OK.
